pr.title: Don't project into `NonNull` when dropping a `Box`
pr.description:
Another step towards banning these projections.

Tracking Issue #133652
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR does not change observable drop semantics; it changes how ElaborateDrops forms the Box interior place. In the old MIR, the drop target is reached by projecting through `Unique.0`/`NonNull.0` and dereferencing that pointer field. In the new MIR, the same `NonNull` value is transmuted/copied into a patch-added `*const T` temporary, and then that temporary is dereferenced. Both paths compute and dereference the identical interior pointer, retain the same partial-move guard (`switchInt(copy _5)`) and cleanup/unwind behavior, and drop the same `(*PTR)` value. The `place_ty`/`MirPatch::local_ty` change exists only because the new code introduces a patch-local pointer temporary; the old code introduced no such local, so it did not hit that lookup path. Therefore no concrete input can distinguish the two versions by a numeric/boolean/character result: the added mir-opt test checks MIR shape (`*const String` temp, transmute, `drop((*_10))`), not runtime output. Any Rust pair made to return different values for the same drop would have to introduce an unrelated semantic change (e.g. dropping a different field, skipping the partial-move guard, or altering the box), which the PR does not justify.

analysis.originalLogic: In `ElaborateDrops` / `elaborate_drop.rs`, when elaborating the drop of a `Box<T>`, the old code built the interior drop place as a chain of projections: `unique_place = field(box_place, 0)`, `nonnull_place = field(unique_place, 0)`, `ptr_place = field(nonnull_place, 0)`, then `interior = deref(ptr_place)`, and passed that projected place to `drop_subpath`. Type lookup in the elaborator's `place_ty` used only `place.ty(self.elaborator.body(), self.tcx())`, which consults `body.local_decls` and therefore cannot resolve locals that exist only in a `MirPatch`. The PR title states the intent: "Don't project into `NonNull` when dropping a `Box`", "Another step towards banning these projections."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, the Box-drop elaboration created a place that projected through the `NonNull` field and dereferenced it directly, represented in the old implementation by `let ptr_place = self.tcx().mk_place_field(nonnull_place, FieldIdx::ZERO, ptr_ty);` followed by `let interior = self.tcx().mk_place_deref(ptr_place);`. That is the wrong transformation to preserve: the drop target should not be a place projection into `NonNull`. The replacement creates a temporary raw-pointer local (`let ptr_local = self.new_temp(ptr_ty);`), emits `Rvalue::Cast(CastKind::Transmute, Operand::Copy(nonnull_place), ptr_ty)` into it, and dereferences `Place::from(ptr_local)`. The old `place_ty` lookup is also insufficient for patch-added locals; the new code explicitly handles that with `self.elaborator.patch_ref().local_ty(place.local)` and `multi_projection_ty`, with the source comment: "We don't have a slice with all the locals, since some are in the patch."
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions containing a dropped `Box<T>` whose drop elaboration reaches the `Unique`/`NonNull` representation, including an ordinary full drop and a conditional/partial move out of the box. The added regression covers `fn maybe_move(cond: bool, thing: Box<String>) -> Option<String>` with `if cond { Some(*thing) } else { None }`; the existing `box_expr.main` case covers a full drop. Cleanup/unwind paths are relevant, and the new test declares `//@ needs-unwind`.
analysis.summary: ElaborateDrops should drop the interior of a Box by loading its NonNull pointer and transmuting it to `*const T` in a new temporary local, then dereferencing that temporary, rather than forming a MIR place projection into the NonNull field. Because the pointer temporary is added by MirPatch, any type query on it must resolve through the patch's new-local table, not only `body.local_decls`. Regression MIR tests assert the raw-pointer temporary and `drop((*PTR))`, and preserve partial-move initialization checks and unwind cleanup.
analysis.trigger: `ElaborateDrops` elaborates a `Box<T>` drop (including a partially moved box), so it constructs the interior drop place from the box's `Unique`/`NonNull` storage; the pass also creates a new `*const T` temporary in the `MirPatch`.
preconditions: The `ElaborateDrops` MIR pass is running on a function that drops a `Box<T>` or drop glue that reaches this Box-drop elaboration path.
The box may have been partially moved, so the drop must retain initialization/partial-move checks before dropping the interior.
Cleanup/unwind edges can be present; the added regression uses `//@ needs-unwind`.
A `MirPatch` may introduce locals that are absent from `body.local_decls`, so their types must be obtained from the patch.
pitfalls: Do not represent the Box interior as a projection through `NonNull` fields such as `((_2.0).0).0`; the PR is explicitly removing such projections: "Another step towards banning these projections."
Do not call ordinary `place.ty(body, tcx)` for a patch-added local; `body.local_decls` does not contain it. Use the patch local type and project from there.
Do not lose the partial-move guard: the corrected MIR still contains `switchInt(copy _5)` before deciding whether to drop the interior.
Do not conflate the new raw-pointer temporary with the Box local itself; the transmute copies the `NonNull` value into a separate `*const T` local.
Do not assume test-file name or old comments prove behavior; compare the actual assignments in the decoded MIR revisions.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused `tests/mir-opt` coverage using `//@ test-mir-pass: ElaborateDrops` and `//@ needs-unwind`. For a conditional partial move from `Box<String>`, emit the `ElaborateDrops` diff and CHECK for a temporary of type `*const std::string::String`, its assignment via `... as *const std::string::String (Transmute)` from the `NonNull`, and `drop((*[[PTR]]))`. Also update the existing full-drop `box_expr.main.ElaborateDrops.diff` expectation to include the new `*const S` local and cleanup block containing the transmute. Verify that no drop path projects directly through `NonNull`, while retaining `switchInt(copy _5)` and unwind cleanup blocks.
evidence: Don't project into `NonNull` when dropping a `Box`
